\begin{enumerate}
\item Let $A=\left\{ a,b,c,d\right\} $ and $B=\left\{ a,b,e,f,g\right\} $

\begin{enumerate}
\item Find $A\cap B$
\item Find $A\cup B$.
\item Find $B-A$.
\item Find $A-B$.\vfill
\end{enumerate}
\item Let $A$ be a nonempty subset of $B$.

\begin{enumerate}
\item Prove that $A\cup B=B$.
\item Prove that generally $A\cap B=B$ is false.\vfill
\end{enumerate}
\item Let $A=\left\{ 1,2,3\right\} $ and $B=\left\{ x,y,z\right\} $.

\begin{enumerate}
\item Find all possible subsets of $A$.
\item List 2 elements in $A\times B$.\vfill
\end{enumerate}
\item Prove that $A\cup\emptyset=A$.\vfill
\item Prove that $A\cap\emptyset=\emptyset$.\vfill
\item Consider the map $f:\mathbb{R}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$ where $f(x)=2x+1$.
Prove that $f$ is onto.\vfill
\item Define the relation $\mathcal{R}$ on the real number set $\mathbb{R}$
as $x\mathcal{R}y\iff x\geq y$. 

\begin{enumerate}
\item Show that $\mathcal{R}$ is reflexive 
\item Show that $\mathcal{R}$ is symmetric.
\item Show that $\mathcal{R}$ is transitive. 
\item Is $\mathcal{R}$ an equivalence relation?\vfill
\end{enumerate}
\item Give an example of a relation which is not transitive.\vfill
\item Let $X$ be a nonempty set. Define the following relation on the set
of subsets of $X$ as follows $A\mathcal{R}B\iff A\cap B\neq\emptyset$
for $A,B\subseteq X$. Prove that $\mathcal{R}$ is not reflexive.
\vfill
\item Let $f:A\rightarrow B$ and $g:B\rightarrow C$ be two functions.

\begin{enumerate}
\item Suppose that $\left|A\right|>\left|B\right|$. Prove that $f$ is
not one-to-one.
\item Suppose that $\left|A\right|<\left|B\right|$. Is $f$ onto? 
\item Is $g\circ f$ onto then is $g$ onto? is $f$ onto? \vfill\newpage
\end{enumerate}
\item Let $S_{3}$ be the symmetric group on three elements. 

\begin{enumerate}
\item Is $S_{3}$ abelian?
\item Is $S_{3}$ cyclic? 
\item Prove that $S_{3}$ has an abelian subgroup.
\item Prove that $S_{3}$ has a non-abelian subgroup.
\item What is the order of $S_{n}$. \vfill
\end{enumerate}
\item Give the definition of homomorphism, and show by example that $f\colon\mathbb{R}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$
where $f(x)=2x$ is a group homomorphism (under addition). \vfill
\item Let $f:G_{1}\rightarrow G_{2}$ be a group homomorphism and let $H\leq G_{2}$.
Recall that $f^{-1}(H)=\left\{ g\in G_{1}|f(g)\in H\right\} $. Prove
that $f^{-1}(H)\leq G_{2}$. \vfill
\item Let $G$ be a finite group of order $24$ and $g\in G$. 

\begin{enumerate}
\item List the \emph{possible }orders of $g$. 
\item Let $H$ be a subset of $G$ such that $\left|H\right|=7$. Is $H\leq G$?
\item Let $\left|H\right|=8$. Does Lagrange's theorem imply that $H\leq G$?\vfill
\end{enumerate}
\item Let $G$ be a group of order $4$. Prove that $G$ is abelian. \vfill
\item Let $G$ be a group where $0_{G}$ is the identity.

\begin{enumerate}
\item Find a subgroup of $G$.
\item Find a subgroup of $G$ distinct from the group given for part \textbf{(a)}.
\item If $\left|G\right|=10$ and $H\leq G$. Prove that $\left|H\right|\neq6$
\vfill
\end{enumerate}
\item Let $H$ and $K$ be subgroups be non-trivial subgroups of $G$. Prove
that $H\cap K$ is a subgroup of $G$.
\item Let $R$ be a ring and $a,b\in R$. 

\begin{enumerate}
\item Which statement is true?

\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{(a)}]If $ab=0$ then $a=0$ or $b=0$.
\item \textbf{(b)}]If $a^{2}=0$ then $a=0$.
\item \textbf{(c)}]If $a\neq0$ and $b\neq0$ then $ab\neq0$.
\item \textbf{(d)}]None of the above.\vfill
\end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}
\item Prove that $\mathbb{Z}$, the set of integers, is a ring under addition
and multiplication. \vfill
\end{enumerate}
